transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we get into the details of the "Tidal Memory" installation plan for Gallery 4, I want to make sure we go through our standard final check today. As you all know, I'm the one who signs off on the public opening plan, and our process calls for the rights, technical, accessibility, and artist representatives to state any conditions that need to be added before I can approve this. So let's hear from each of you — are there any conditions or concerns we need to address regarding the current draft? For reference, the draft proposes online-connected playback, eight visitor stations, 15-minute sessions, and a 5:00 PM public opening on October 12. Please go ahead.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I reviewed the countersigned music license this morning, and I need to flag several conditions that must be added to the exhibition plan before it can be approved. The license restricts Tidal Memory to offline local playback only — so the current draft's proposal of online-connected playback is not permitted. Additionally, visitors may not photograph or record the installation, and the exact credit line 'Music licensed from Harborlight Editions' must be used. I haven't amended the exhibition packet yet because the license arrived after the packet was circulated, but these conditions need to be incorporated before Maya signs off.

transcript.text: I need to flag a technical condition based on the headset and network test I completed after yesterday's installation rehearsal. The approved headset model supports only six simultaneous stations — not eight as the draft proposes — and each session must be limited to exactly 12 minutes to prevent thermal shutdown. So the current draft's proposal of eight stations and 15-minute sessions is not technically viable. I should also note that the test report is still sitting in the equipment vendor's queue, so it hasn't been formally circulated yet, but these are hard constraints we need to incorporate into the plan before approval.

transcript.text: I have an accessibility condition to add before this plan can be approved. I confirmed today with the festival's access consultant that one of the six visitor stations must be a seated, step-free station. Additionally, every visitor notice must display the exact warning 'Flashing light and sudden sound.' I should note that the consultant's written confirmation was received after the draft visitor signage was already sent to print, so the printed signage will need to be corrected before opening.
